matter.title: Helios Renewables Pvt. Ltd. v. Northgrid Power Ltd.

entries.text: **Article 113** of the Limitation Act, 1963 prescribes a **three-year** period for suits for which no other period is provided, from when the right to sue accrues. The plaint relies on this (**Plaint ¶15, p. 3**).
**Section 12A** requires pre-institution mediation for commercial disputes. The plaint references this (**Plaint ¶12, p. 3**).

**PPA** dated **14.08.2021** between Helios Renewables (Seller) and Northgrid Power (Buyer) for 12 MW solar plant at Bhadla, Rajasthan, for 25 years at fixed tariff of **Rs. 2.95 per kWh** (**Plaint ¶3, p. 1**; **PPA p. 1**).

**Clause 9.1:** monthly invoice on JMR signed by both parties. **Clause 9.2:** payment within **30 days** of receipt. **Clause 9.3:** if JMR not signed within 7 days, SLDC reading final. **Clause 9.4:** dispute must be notified in writing within **15 days**; undisputed amount paid; if not disputed within 15 days, invoice deemed accepted. **Clause 9.6:** late payment surcharge **1% per month** simple (**PPA pp. 1-2**).

**Clause 14.1:** Buyer to establish and maintain a revolving **Letter of Credit of Rs. 6,00,00,000** before COD. **Clause 14.2:** failure to renew within 7 days of written demand is a **Buyer Event of Default** (**PPA p. 2**).

**Clause 16.1:** Buyer Event of Default includes (a) failure to pay undisputed invoice within **60 days** of Due Date; (b) failure to maintain LC. **Clause 16.3:** cure period of **60 days** after default notice. **Clause 16.4:** termination does not affect accrued rights (**PPA p. 2**).

**Clause 17.1:** Change in Law defined. **Clause 17.2:** affected party must give notice within **30 days**; parties negotiate tariff adjustment; Change in Law alone does not permit termination (**PPA pp. 2-3**).

**Clause 18.1:** Force Majeure defined. **Clause 18.2:** notice within **7 days**. **Clause 18.3:** if FM continues >180 days, either party may terminate with **30 days** notice. **Clause 18.5:** FM does not excuse payment for energy already supplied (**PPA p. 3**).

**Clause 22.1:** parties attempt amicable resolution through senior officers within **30 days** of written notice. **Clause 22.2:** unresolved disputes referred to **arbitration** by sole arbitrator under Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, seat New Delhi. **Clause 22.3:** tariff disputes to appropriate Electricity Regulatory Commission. **Clause 22.4:** pending dispute, parties continue performance and Buyer pays undisputed amounts (**PPA pp. 3-4**).
**Clause 23.2:** subject to Clause 22, courts at **New Delhi** have exclusive jurisdiction (**PPA p. 4**).
The Plant achieved **Commercial Operation Date (COD)** on **06.12.2021** (**Plaint ¶4, p. 2**).
Northgrid paid **Rs. 36,80,000** against the February 2023 invoice on **28.03.2023** (**Plaint ¶5, p. 2**).
The invoice for **April 2023** (first of ten invoices from April 2023 to 09.01.2024) fell due on **05.05.2023** and was not paid (**Plaint ¶¶6-7, pp. 2-3**; cause of action ¶14, p. 3).
Helios sent the first of several email reminders to Northgrid between **16.05.2023** and **20.12.2023** (**Plaint ¶7, p. 2**; **Annexure P-4**).
In an email dated **14.07.2023**, Northgrid stated payments were 'kept under review' on account of grid curtailment, but did not dispute any invoice (**Plaint ¶7, p. 2**).
Northgrid claims the Plant suffered a major outage between **02.08.2023** and **19.08.2023**, and that Helios billed for energy not supplied during that period (**Reply to notice ¶3, p. 2**).
Northgrid allowed the **Letter of Credit** to lapse on **30.09.2023** and did not renew it despite Helios' request (**Plaint ¶9, p. 2**; **Legal notice ¶4, p. 1**).
Northgrid's officers informed Helios' site team on **08.11.2023** that the meter readings for October 2023 were not accepted (**Reply to notice ¶2, p. 2**).
Northgrid's officers again informed Helios' site team on **12.12.2023** that the readings for November 2023 were not accepted (**Reply to notice ¶2, p. 2**).

Northgrid issued a notice dated **09.01.2024** purporting to terminate the PPA on grounds of **Change in Law** and **Force Majeure**, citing increase in inter-state transmission charges notified in 2023 (**Plaint ¶10, p. 3**; **Annexure P-5**).

Helios, through counsel, issued a legal notice dated **02.02.2024** demanding payment of **Rs. 3,68,40,000** (principal) plus late payment surcharge at **1% per month** under Clause 9.6, within 15 days (**Legal notice pp. 1-2**; **Plaint ¶11, p. 3**).

Northgrid replied on **21.02.2024** denying liability: disputed invoices for Oct-Dec 2023 (JMR not signed), claimed outage, said LC lapse due to Change in Law/FM, and invoked **Clause 22** for arbitration (**Reply to notice pp. 2-3**; **Plaint ¶11, p. 3**).

Helios initiated pre-institution mediation under **Section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015** before the Delhi High Court Mediation and Conciliation Centre on **14.10.2024** (**Plaint ¶12, p. 3**).
Northgrid did not appear despite notice; a **non-starter report** was issued on **18.12.2024** (**Plaint ¶12, p. 3**; **Annexure P-8**).
Helios' Board of Directors passed a resolution on **24.02.2025** authorising Mr. Arvind Mehra to sign, verify and institute the suit (**Plaint ¶1, p. 1**).

Helios filed **CS(COMM) 412 of 2025** in the High Court of Delhi seeking recovery of **Rs. 4,82,00,000** (principal **Rs. 3,74,00,000** plus interest **Rs. 1,08,00,000** at 18% p.a.), and a declaration that the termination notice is illegal (**Plaint pp. 1-4**).

inSum: Helios Renewables and Northgrid Power signed a PPA on 14.08.2021 for a 12 MW solar plant. Helios achieved COD on 06.12.2021 and was paid regularly until March 2023. From April 2023, Northgrid stopped paying ten invoices totalling Rs. 3,74,00,000. Northgrid allowed the required Letter of Credit to lapse on 30.09.2023 and later terminated the PPA on 09.01.2024 citing Change in Law and Force Majeure. Helios sent a legal notice on 02.02.2024; Northgrid replied on 21.02.2024 denying liability, disputing invoices (claiming JMR not signed and an outage), and invoking arbitration. Pre-institution mediation failed on 18.12.2024. Helios filed the present suit on 06.03.2025 claiming Rs. 4,82,00,000 (principal plus interest). The suit is pending.

limitation.headline: First unpaid invoice due 05.05.2023 → 3 years ends 05.05.2026
limitation.note: The suit was filed on 06.03.2025, which is within three years from the due date of the first unpaid invoice (05.05.2023). However, Northgrid may argue that limitation runs from each invoice's due date separately, and that the last invoice (for December 2023/January 2024) fell due later. The plaint relies on Article 113 of the Limitation Act, 1963. Please check with your advocate.
